sentences.text: Paraisurus was a member of the class Chondrichthyes, a group that includes sharks, rays, and skates.
Four valid species of Paraisurus have been found in Europe, Asia, North America, and Australia.
Paraisurus went extinct around the Albian-Cenomanian boundary, and a supposed Coniacian occurrence is likely a misidentified pseudoscapanorhynchid.
The parent group of Paraisurus is Paraisuridae, and the animal belongs to the family Paraisuridae.
This animal lived from the Aptian to the Cenomanian, between 121.4 and 93.9 million years ago.
The status of P. amudarjensis is debated, with some paleontologists considering it a possible synonym of P. compressus.
